edu.title: How Lexicamp works
edu.teaser: The science behind your climb — tap to learn more.
edu.s1Body: Lexicamp schedules every word with FSRS, a modern spaced-repetition algorithm. It models how your memory of each word strengthens over time and plans the next review for the moment you're about to forget — so you study less and remember more.
edu.s2Body: Each saved word carries a predicted recall strength. When that strength drops toward the point of forgetting, the word becomes due and joins your study session. Recalling it correctly pushes the next review further out; missing it brings the word back sooner.
edu.s3Title: Getting the most out of it
edu.s3Body: Study a little every day instead of cramming, and rate yourself honestly — the schedule is only as good as your feedback. Short, consistent sessions move words up the mountain from Base Camp to Summit.

masteryCard.tierInfoTitle: Each word has its own tier
masteryCard.tierInfoContent: Every word progresses from Base Camp → Summit upon review, based on its FSRS stability. Tap any tier segment for details.
masteryCard.summitInfoContent: Words at Summit have ≥ 30-day FSRS stability. They exit your active review queue and count as fully mastered.

progress.title: Progress
progress.fullRouteSub: Summit at the top. Keep climbing.
progress.wordsByTierSub: How well your {{count}} saved words are retained
progress.cefrIntro: The Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR) defines six proficiency levels. Lexicamp maps your saved-word count to an approximate CEFR level as you climb the mountain.
progress.cefrNote: CEFR labels are approximate. Lexicamp counts individual word forms, so thresholds are compressed from research baselines.
progress.fsrsIntro: Every saved word is scored by the FSRS algorithm. Its stability (in days) reflects how long your memory will hold before the next optimal review.
progress.fsrsNote: A word is mastered at 30+ days of stability. This same threshold gates your mountain-tier progression.
